before:
Fenside Reed-Cutters' Association — Committee Notes, 14 February

The committee reviewed the allocation of the shared punt for the cutting season. Members present agreed that the existing sequence should stand: bank stabilisation work is served before thatching orders, and thatching orders before visitor demonstrations. All three uses remain open to any member in good standing, and no application is refused on grounds of purpose. The warden will continue to enter each booking in the shed diary. Where two requests arrive on the same morning, the warden applies the sequence above and reports the outcome to the next meeting. Nothing in this arrangement alters the hours during which the punt may be taken out.

before:
Harbour Slipway Manual — Section 4: Winch House Access

The winch house is opened by the duty keeper at first light and closed after the last recovery of the day. Key holders may operate the winch single-handed outside the published tide windows. A second person stands at the head of the slip whenever a trailer is on the ramp, and the drum brake is tested before each lift. Hard hats are worn inside the winch house at all times. The keeper enters the meter figure in the wall book at close of day. Grease is applied to the gearing every fourth week, or sooner if the cable runs noisy.
after:
Harbour Slipway Manual — Section 4: Winch House Access

Key holders are forbidden to operate the winch single-handed outside the published tide windows. A second person stands at the head of the slip whenever a trailer is on the ramp, and the drum brake is tested before each lift. Hard hats are worn inside the winch house at all times. variation_site: The change falls in the sentence about single-handed winching outside tide windows.
author_note: Turns a permission into a prohibition with no other content disturbed.

before:

The autumn work party has been completed and the following notes are issued to all subscribers. Members are respectfully reminded that the stove flue at Cairn Dubh has been swept and that the woodshed is stocked to the roof. Water is drawn from the burn above the crossing, not below it. before:
County Herbarium — Accession Catalogue, Sheet 44

Accession 4417 was gathered on the dune slack at Sennen Warren in July and mounted the following week. The sheet is filed as Carex arenaria and stands in the sedge cabinet under that heading. Collector's notes give the substrate as damp shell sand over a thin humus layer, and the gathering as a single tussock with runners. The sheet bears the original field label, a determination slip, and a barcode in the lower right corner. Loans are made to institutional borrowers only, and the sheet must travel in a rigid folder. A duplicate went to the regional collection in the same season.

The yew by the north gate is believed, on the evidence of a single girth measurement, to be around four hundred years old, and an arborist will inspect the crown before any path widening begins. The gravel walk from the lychgate to the chapel steps will be relaid in the same material. Holders wishing to place temporary edging should speak to the sexton first. Watering cans are kept by the standpipe and returned to the rack. The gate is locked at dusk from October, and the key is held at the parish office.

before:
Inshore Rescue Handbook — Appendix C: Station Distances

This appendix collects the fixed distances used when estimating passage times from the station. The distance from the boathouse to the outer perch is measured at 1.4 nautical miles, taken along the marked channel rather than across the sands. The perch to the wreck buoy adds a further half mile, and the wreck buoy to the harbour entrance a mile and a quarter. Crews should treat these figures as a planning aid only, since the channel shifts after heavy weather. Passage times are worked at the boat's cruising speed with an allowance for tide. The appendix is checked against the annual survey each spring.

before:
Community Laundry — Handling of Returned Items

This document covers items brought back to the counter after a machine cycle. Items are weighed, then sorted by fabric, then tagged with the member's number before they go to the drying room. Any garment showing dye transfer is set aside for the supervisor, who decides whether a refund is due. Members are entitled to a free rewash where a fault in the machine is established. The counter book is kept in ink and totals are carried forward weekly. Nothing here removes a member's right to complain to the management committee, whose decision on refunds is final. Unclaimed items are held for six weeks.

before:
Millpond Footbridge — Condition Report, Third Inspection

The deck boards were sounded and four were found soft at the bearer line. Allowable loading for the repaired span is worked out using the county surveyor's timber tables of 1974, giving the working figure that the parish has adopted for its signage. The handrail was found sound throughout, with two loose standards to be reset. Silt has built against the upstream pier and should be raked clear before the winter flows. The inspector recommends a further visit in eighteen months, or sooner if further boards go soft. Photographs are appended and all measurements were taken by tape from the downstream abutment.

before:
Tide Gauge Feed — Station Configuration

This file governs how the gauge at the east pier writes its half-hourly output to the archive drive. Each reading is emitted as one line, with fields given as station|datetime|height|quality and no trailing separator. Heights are in metres above chart datum to two decimal places, and the quality flag is a single letter. The archive rolls at midnight and the previous day's file is compressed and kept for seven years. If the gauge loses power the buffer holds four hours of readings and replays them on restart. Nothing here alters what the gauge measures or how often it reports.

before:
Seed Bank — Germination Testing Procedure

For the purposes of this document a testing season is the twelve months beginning on 1 October. Every accession is tested once per season, viability is reported as a season average, and the storage review takes the two most recent seasons together. Trays are sown in fives and held at the bench temperature stated on the accession card. Counts are made at seven, fourteen and twenty-one days by the technician on duty. Where germination falls below half the accession's first measured figure, regeneration is scheduled in the following season. Bench notes are kept in the laboratory book and totals transferred to the accession card.

before:
Common Grazing Registry — Standing Conditions

The registry lists shareholders, their souming, and the conditions attached to each holding. Shareholders may keep a pony on the common without further application, provided the animal is shod and marked. Stock is turned out after the twelfth of May and gathered before the first frosts. Fencing along the burn is maintained by the shareholders whose ground abuts it, in equal shares of labour. Dogs are worked only by their handlers. Entries are amended at the annual meeting and the clerk issues an updated sheet to each shareholder. Disputes over souming go to the grazings committee before any other body is approached.
after:
Common Grazing Registry — Standing Conditions

The registry lists shareholders, their souming, and the conditions attached to each holding. Shareholders may not keep a pony on the common without the written consent of the clerk, provided the animal is shod and marked. Stock is turned out after the twelfth of May and gathered before the first frosts. Fencing along the burn is maintained by the shareholders whose ground abuts it, in equal shares of labour. Dogs are worked only by their handlers. Entries are amended at the annual meeting and the clerk issues an updated sheet to each shareholder. Disputes over souming go to the grazings committee before any other body is approached.
variation_site: The change falls in the sentence about ponies on the common.
author_note: A standing permission becomes a conditional prohibition requiring consent.
